name: The Artefact
description: A broken chronicle that woke at Copenhagen Airport. It does not teach Japanese. It asks the family to notice things and fill the gaps.

name: Hinomaru
description: The sun disc. Japan’s name, Nihon, means origin of the sun. The flag is not a sunset. It is a claim about where light begins.

name: Depachika
description: The city under the city: department-store basements packed with food. Tokyo stacked itself on old wetland. The sky is optional.

name: The Unthirsty Machine
description: Vending machines that sell eggs, umbrellas, manga or hot food. A city that stays open after the staff go home.

name: Onigiri
description: A rice triangle wrapped in nori. Konbini food is how a megacity eats at odd hours — not a compromise, a system.

name: Maneki-neko
description: The beckoning cat. The raised paw is an invitation, not a wave. Folklore says one cat saved a lord from lightning.

name: 634 / Musashi
description: Tokyo Skytree is 634 metres tall because 6-3-4 can be read mu-sa-shi, the old provincial name. A lightning rod that is also a word.

name: Kitsune
description: Fox spirits. Messengers of Inari. Statues hold a key, a jewel or rice. Farmers once left the first harvest for them.

name: Torii
description: A gate that marks the start of sacred ground. At Fushimi Inari the tunnel of gates is a ledger: each one paid for by a family or a company.

name: Matcha
description: Powdered green tea. Monks used it to stay awake. The sweet on the tray exists because the tea is severe.

name: Ekiben
description: A packed train lunch. The box is the point: a meal that can leave with you.

name: Temizu
description: A water basin by the shrine path. Hands and mouth are rinsed before you step closer.
